correctness.rationale: The invariant graph and vertices were checked against Cima et al. §5.7 and Appendix Figs. 60–61. Direct affine endpoint substitution gives the eight core images in the repaired proof. Outside the core, [Z_1,X_3] maps into [X_1,Z_2], which maps onto the collapsing [X_2,Z_3]; the extra first-quadrant diagonal through S collapses to P_1. Thus no positive-length escaping branch contributes an additional survivor subsystem. The three core cycles all pass through C. Starting there and writing t=2u+b+2 gives the second iterate (t,b−1−t) in the core. The three full return domains in t are [0,b/2], [b,3b/2], [(7b−4)/8,b−1/2], with resulting first coordinates 2t−b, 2t−3b, 7b−8t−4. The last interval stays in I because b≤4 and enters the noncollapsing D part after B; the second fits G because b≤4; the first fits H because b≥2. Endpoint coincidences at b=2,3,4 leave the nondegenerate interiors and gaps intact. The two gaps in u are (3b−4)/16≥1/8 and 1/4, and the similarity ratios give both b(9/16)^k and the dimension equation 2·4^(−s)+16^(−s)=1. Preimages of finitely many partition vertices along noncollapsing prefixes are countable; histories that enter a constant branch are already excluded. The Cantor subset and its countably many noncollapsing affine preimages establish the claimed dimension on the entire graph, with isolated points harmless. No uploaded code was executed.
